subject: Inference service event — customer-facing recap and remediation timeline
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@clearstream.com>, ops@clearstream.com
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com, grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Inference service event — initial customer-facing recap and artifacts

Jordan / Clearstream ops team,

Thanks again for your patience this morning. We completed our internal forensics and wanted to share a consolidated, customer-facing recap of the event, a short timeline showing when impact occurred, and the near-term remediation plan we will execute together. Attached are: clearstream_event_timeline.csv (hit/response times and request IDs), root-analysis-20261116.pdf (technical findings and contributing factors), and mitigation-checklist.xlsx (action owners and deadlines).

High-level recap:
- Impact window: 2026-11-16 08:03–08:41 PST.
- Observable customer symptoms: elevated token latency for batch inference and ~1.2% request failures for requests routed to the legacy quantized variant.
- Root analysis summary: a cascading KV-cache eviction combined with an outdated kernel selection path on an older GPU variant caused persistent longer tail latency and a subset of tokenization mismatches. The attached document explains the chain of events.

Immediate actions we are taking (next 72 hours):
1) Replace routing policy for your account to the newer model variant with verified kernel paths (owner: Naomi) — ETA 12 hours.
2) Apply conservative cache eviction guardrails to restore expected KV hit rates (owner: Grace) — ETA 24 hours.
3) Run a verification sweep on queued requests and replayed traffic to validate outputs against golden prompts (owner: Rachel) — ETA 48 hours.

We also included recommended compensatory controls for longer-term resilience. We propose a short technical briefing at 10:30 PST today to walk through the artifacts and confirm owners. Please let me know if that time works or share an alternate.

We recognize the disruption this caused for Clearstream's peak batch window and will follow up with a written verification note after the actions complete.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Account Lead, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
attachments: clearstream_event_timeline.csv, root-analysis-20261116.pdf, mitigation-checklist.xlsx
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@clearstream.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Inference service event — initial customer-facing recap and artifacts

Rachel — thanks for the prompt recap and the artifacts. A few quick clarifications from our side: 
- Can you confirm whether any customer data was included in the logs you attached? We need to verify PII exposure policies.
- The timeline shows an earlier spike at 07:58 PST; did you see anything indicating a precursor event?
- For the verification sweep, can we request a scoped replay focused on our top 10 production prompts only? That keeps the scope small and actionable.

10:30 works for a short call for Jordan / ops team. One ask for the call: please have a senior engineer on the kernel/runtime side join (if possible Naomi or Grace).

—Jordan
Jordan Lee
Head of Platform Ops
Clearstream Payments
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@clearstream.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com, grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Inference service event — initial customer-facing recap and artifacts

Jordan — quick replies inline: 
- Logs: the attached CSV and the technical PDF contain aggregated telemetry and anonymized request IDs only. No raw customer payloads or PII fields are present; we redacted any user identifiers during extraction. We will share a sanitized verification report post-sweep.
- Precursor spike at 07:58 PST: good catch — that was a short-lived degradation in the autoscaler signalling on a minority of nodes which increased batch sizes momentarily; that upstream condition amplified the KV eviction behavior 5 minutes later. We describe this in section 2.1 of the PDF.
- Replay scope: yes — we will run a scoped replay on your top 10 prompts and include a diff report for semantic drift or tokenization differences. Owner: Rachel.

Call attendees: Naomi (runtime kernels) and Grace (serving/runtime ops) will join. Proposed agenda: 1) Walk timeline & findings (10 mins), 2) Confirm immediate mitigations and owners (10 mins), 3) Verification plan & acceptance criteria (10 mins).

I will post the call invite and a shared Drive link with the sanitized artifacts. Thanks — we want to make this as transparent and low-friction as possible.

Rachel
attachments: none
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@clearstream.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: verification results and next steps (post-call)

Jordan / Clearstream ops / Rachel — following our 10:30 briefing and the scoped replay we completed this afternoon, quick status update and the next milestones: 

Summary of verification (short):
- Replay scope: your top 10 production prompts across the 08:00–09:00 PST window.
- Findings: output parity achieved for 98/100 sampled requests; two cases showed tokenization boundary shifts on the legacy quantized variant only (no semantic regressions).
- Latency: median latency returned to baseline after routing policy change; P95 improved once cache guardrails were applied.

Completed actions (today):
- Account routing switched to the vetted model variant (complete).
- Cache eviction guardrails applied to serving layer — guardrails tuned to preserve KV residency for sequences matching your workload (complete).
- Scoped replay executed; results stored in Drive link.

Planned actions (owners & windows):
- 72-hour stress run across staged traffic with full tracing enabled (owner: Grace; ETA: 72 hours).
- Backfill of kernel selection tests into our nightly regression suite to prevent reintroduction (owner: Naomi; ETA: 7 days).
- Customer verification package and signed acceptance checklist (owner: Rachel; ETA: 48 hours).

We will also provide a short audit-ready log bundle for your compliance team once the stress run completes. If you want that delivered earlier, tell us and we will prioritize.

Naomi Feldman
Senior Runtime Engineer
Redwood Inference
attachments: verification-summary-20261116.txt (sanitized), SUP-4789-trace-ids.csv
